plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with high probability, and minimize overpayment, I will bid slightly above this. A bid of $33.00 seems reasonable.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any bid above that point risks overpaying, and any bid below risks letting the item go for less than its worth. Since this is round 1 with no history, I will implement this strategy. My value is $34, so 2/3 * $34 = $22.67. I will round this to the nearest tenth.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation below your value risks losing the auction when it's profitable to win, and bidding above your value risks overpaying. Since this is round 1, and there's no history, I will bid my true value of $45.
